target.title: fix(media-core): detect MIME from encoded URL extensions
target.body:
Fixes encoded HTTP(S) media URLs such as `render%2Emp4` being treated as unknown by the media-core MIME fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users or plugins that pass media URLs with percent-encoded extension separators could get an unknown MIME result when the URL still points to a supported file type.

For example, a normal URL such as:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4?download=1
```

is classified as `video/mp4`, but the encoded-path equivalent:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1
```

misses the `.mp4` extension because the URL pathname remains percent-encoded before `path.extname()` runs. That affects the shared `mimeTypeFromFilePath()` / `detectMime({ filePath })` fallback used by media callers when no stronger MIME signal is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior scoped to HTTP(S) URL pathname extension lookup in `getFileExtension()`. It decodes the URL pathname before extracting the extension, and falls back to the original pathname if the URL contains malformed percent encoding.

This does not add a shared filename decoder, does not parse `Content-Disposition`, and does not change the local path fallback. It only makes encoded URL pathnames follow the same MIME classification path as the equivalent decoded URL path.

## User Impact

Media URLs whose path encodes the extension dot can now be classified like their ordinary URL equivalents.

Examples that now flow through the expected media MIME fallback:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1 -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm             -> video/webm
```

That helps downstream media handling choose the correct behavior when a CDN or provider returns encoded URL path components.

## Evidence

Behavior proof from current `main` before this change:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4?download=1  -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1 -> undefined
https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm             -> undefined
```

Focused coverage now exercises the shared media-core fallback instead of a provider-specific wrapper:

```text
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm") === "video/webm"
detectMime({ filePath: "https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1" }) === "video/mp4"
```

Validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       104 passed (104)

git diff --check
passed
```
